To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2x exchanger (NClx) is distributed asymmetrically across the mitochondrial surface and is largely absent from the mitochondrial junctional SR (jSfR) contact sites, where mitochondrial Ca2+ is received from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2 exchanger is targeted to non-junctional mitochondrial domains, and that the distribution of this protein and the uniporter channel complex are reciprocally organized to optimize energy efficiency.

the mitochondrial Ca2+-transporting machinery is spatially segregated to different mitochondrial domains, with the mitochondrial Ca2 + uniporter forming hotspots at the junctional SR (j SR) and the Na+/Ca 2 + exchanger forming non-j SR-associated hotspots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial separation of Ca2+ uptake (MCUC) and extrusion (NCLX) in mitochondria.

the mechanisms that regulate mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling in cardiac myocytes, with the aim of improving our understanding of the molecular basis of Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload in the heart.
the spatial separation of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling in the heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mitochondria are the main site of ATP production in the cell.

mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling is spatially separated from mitochondrial Ca2+ efflux in the heart, with the former occurring in jSR-associated mitochondria and the latter in non-jSR-associated mitochondria, which are also the major sites of ATP production.

the spatial distribution of the mitochondrial Ca2 + uniporter channel complex and of the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2 + exchanger is reciprocally polarised, which is likely to optimize the efficiency of local mitochondrial calcium signalling in the heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial calcium uptake and extrusion processes in cardiac mitochondria are spatially separated.

the mitochondrial Ca2+-handling machinery is spatially segregated in cardiac mitochondria, with Ca2+ uptake localized to the mitochondrial association with the junctional SR and Ca2+ efflux to the cytosol localized to non-junctional SR-associated mitochondria.
mitochondrial calcium uptake and extrusion have different spatial distributions and that this is important for energy efficiency of calcium signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial Ca2+ signals are spatially separated from the sites of Ca2+ extrusions in cardiac mitochondria.
the spatial separation of the two main mechanisms for mitochondrial Ca2+ transport is important to ensure the energy efficiency of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling.

the spatial separation of mitochondrial calcium uptake and extrusion is an important feature of cardiac mitochondrial calcium signaling, and that this separation is achieved by the non-polarized localization of the Na+/Ca 2+ exchanger at the inner mitochondrial membrane.
